title: Lifeboat rollout pocket canvas and hourly telemetry tap
content:
Purpose:
A compact, on-shift pocket guide for the small-batch 'lifeboat' rollout pattern. Designed to fit in an operator's tab during emergency or high-risk feature migrations. This is intentionally terse: step-by-step cues, hourly telemetry checkpoints, quick commands, and a minimal post-release sketch for follow-up.

Quick summary (one-liner):
Patch launches that must stay online with progressive traffic slices + live canary telemetry; immediate lifeboat fallback to previous model/service in <5 minutes if error thresholds are crossed.

When to use this pattern:
- High-caution changes (model routing, KV cache schema, runtime quantization toggles)
- Limited burn-in windows (30–120 minutes) where rollback cost is cheap but user impact is sensitive
- Teams that need a tight hourly observability cadence and a single-operator playbook

Preflight (T-24h to T-1h):
- Confirm deployment artifact and hash: ensure PR + build match (github:repo/infra#PR-1742).
- Smoke test artifact locally against prod-like fixtures (run: scripts/smoke-run.sh --fixtures=prod-2027).
- Check capacity headroom in Dedicated pools: slack #dedicated-ops -> query: /capacity headroom <region>.
- Coordinate with Console on rollout flag: set flag namespace=routing, key=lifeboat-experiment, initial=0.
- Document the release elevator pitch in Jira REL-3421: one paragraph + rollback criterion.
- Assign owner (operator) and backup on-call for next 6 hours.

T-minus 10 minutes (on-call operator checklist):
- Post to #release-ops: "Lifeboat rollout starting: REL-3421, owner=AvaM, ETA 11:20 PT".
- Load quick dashboard: /dash/routing-lifeboat (bookmark: Console -> Favorites -> routing-lifeboat).
- Confirm alert mute windows for noisy canaries (only if noise is expected).
- Open a lightweight incident room: calls: https://meet.company.com/rel-3421 (one-click link).

Deployment steps (T0 -> +15m):
1) Toggle flag to 5% traffic slice (API: POST /flags/set {namespace:routing, key:lifeboat-experiment, value:5})
2) Wait 90s for metrics aggregation.
3) Validate core metrics (see "Hourly telemetry taps" below).
4) If green, move to 25% after 10m. If red, execute Lifeboat fallback (see below).

Lifeboat fallback (immediate action if any gating metric exceeds threshold):
- Command: POST /flags/set {namespace:routing, key:lifeboat-experiment, value:0} (this routes everyone back).
- Confirm rollback by checking traffic distribution in Console (expect 0% variant).
- Short post to #release-ops: "Lifeboat executed: REL-3421 — reason: <metric> exceeded threshold. Timestampped notes attached."
- If rollback fails (traffic doesn't flip): escalate to SRE runbook 7 (networking-edge sanity) and open pager Escalation-2.

Hourly telemetry taps (first 2 hours are high-sensitivity):
- 0m (post-deploy): error-rate-total (5m window) < 0.3% absolute increase vs baseline
- +5m: p95 latency (user-facing API) < baseline + 60ms
- +15m: model-quality proxy (rerank delta) within expected band (see REL-3421 testset)
- +30m: backend CPU/GPU saturations: no single host >80% sustained for 3m
- +60m: use-case QPS breakdown — no region shows >15% deviation from pre-launch distribution
- Operator actions: at each tap, annotate Console with verdict: green/amber/red and a one-sentence rationale.

Gating thresholds (operator quick reference):
- Error rate: >0.5% absolute increase -> red
- Latency: p95 increase >100ms -> amber (investigate), >200ms -> red
- Quality proxy: >2% regression on canary prompt set -> amber -> consider rollback
- Infrastructure: sustained host saturation >85% -> amber -> scale up or rollback

Communication snippets (paste-ready):
- Preflight announce: "Starting lifeboat rollout REL-3421 at T0. Owner: Ava Martinez. Traffic: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> monitor 2h. Post to #release-ops for each gate."
- Lifeboat executed: "Lifeboat fallback triggered for REL-3421 at 11:26 PT. Reason: p95 latency spike to +240ms. Rolling back traffic flag to 0%. Investigating."
- Rollforward success: "REL-3421 reached 50% at 12:15 PT with stable metrics. Scheduling follow-up retro and testset eval."

Quick commands (operator shell cheats):
- set flag: curl -X POST $FLAGS_API -d '{"namespace":"routing","key":"lifeboat-experiment","value":5}' 
- confirm traffic: curl $ROUTE_API/traffic?variant=lifeboat | jq .percent
- tail logs for canary: tail -n 500 /var/log/canary/*.log | grep REL-3421
- force rollback (superuser): ./opsctl lifeboat rollback --ticket REL-3421 --reason "auto-rollback"

Post-release sketch (T+2h -> T+72h):
- 2h: final canary verdict. If green, schedule 24h slow ramp to 100% or to target weight.
- 24h: automated eval runs on production prompts: attach snapshot to REL-3421.
- 72h: close ticket with short notes, link to perf diffs and any incident samplings.

Retro template (fill during postmortem):
- Summary: what shipped and why (1-2 lines)
- Timeline: T0 to T+72h notable events (time, action, owner)
- Signals: list of metrics that mattered and their values at decision points
- What worked: instrumentation, comms, playbook items
- What failed / ambiguous: gaps in observability, confusing alerts, slow rollback actions
- Action items: owner, ETA, verification method

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Consider adding a tiny canary probe that hits the most brittle code path (avoid cold-start artifacts)
- We lack a single CLI command that both toggles flag and posts to #release-ops; could save 30s in a hot rollback
- Investigate using prefix cache snapshotting to speed up recovery post-rollback
- Can we add a short-lived synthetic user journey that runs every 30s in the first hour? pager noise tradeoff.

Open questions for follow-up:
- What's our guardrail for KG-backed rerank regressions? need product sign-off (ping @product-hosted-api).
- SLA implications if lifeboat toggles cause partial failures in dependent services. Draft note to legal/compliance?

Attachments / quick refs:
- REL-3421 (jira) — one-line goal and rollback criteria
- github:repo/infra#PR-1742 — deployment artifact and smoke logs
- Console dashboard link: /dash/routing-lifeboat

If you take anything away from this pocket canvas: be explicit about owner, keep the telemetry taps tight, and make the rollback path a single human action (ideally one API call). This is written to be used while half-asleep at 03:00 shift or under noisy incident conditions.

End of document.
